title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 86
paragraphs: So it was with these. But the greater part of their ships were disabled at Salamis, destroyed some by the Athenians and others by the Aeginetans. For since the Greeks fought in good order and in their assigned places, while the barbarians were no longer in order and did nothing by design, it was likely that such a result would follow. Yet on this day they surpassed themselves far more than when they had fought at Euboea, every man being eager and fearing Xerxes, each thinking that the king's eye was particularly on him.
